Advance Tax: Commercial importers are granted an exemption from paying the five percent Advance Tax at the import stage for specific types of unrefined edible oil. This exemption applies to products classified under the relevant customs heading codes for these specific oils.

The National Board of Revenue has provided an exemption from the five percent advance tax for specific imported crude edible oils under defined conditions. This exemption applies when registered commercial importers import these goods under contract with a refinery, subject to approval and regulatory compliance.
National Board of Revenue: Exercising powers granted under the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act 2012, the National Board of Revenue has issued this order to grant tax relief in the public interest for specific imported commodities.
Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty A: Section 126(3) of this Act serves as the legal foundation authorizing the National Board of Revenue to grant exemptions from the payment of advance tax.
Import Policy Order 2021-2024: This policy permits commercial importers to import specific crude oils under contract with a refinery, provided they obtain prior approval from the Ministry of Commerce. Under these conditions, the commercial importer is officially recognized as an industrial enterprise for the purpose of the import.
